Known, documented, **not fixed** in this pass: `/search` Accessibility sits at 0.91 against the 0.95 threshold — `link-name` (two live-catalog cards with an empty `Movie.name` from the API) and `target-size` (`YearRangeSlider`'s dual-thumb inputs, a documented pattern — see [Component structure](#component-structure)) are real findings, candidates for a separate a11y task, not silently swept under a lowered threshold. This whole table is a local dev-smoke measurement, not the CI gate's baseline — `vite preview` doesn't apply `vercel.json`'s headers, Vercel's CDN compression, or `X-Robots-Tag`.

- **Task 4's live-confirmed facts and what's still deferred to a human.** Confirmed live and for real: `GET /v1.5/movie/666` → `200` (see above); pinned action versions — `patrickedqvist/wait-for-vercel-preview@v1.3.3` (the exact tag, not floating `v1`, because `v1` on this action resolves to an older commit than the real latest release — verified via the GitHub API), `treosh/lighthouse-ci-action@v12` (floating major is safe here — `v12` does resolve to the current release), `actions/github-script@v8`. Still deferred to a human with browser/Vercel-dashboard access, tracked in the plan's Post-Completion: (1) a Vercel dashboard visit to confirm preview deployments register as GitHub Deployments and to check Deployment Protection status; (2) a live `curl -I` against a real preview URL to confirm the assumed `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`; (3) an actual test PR with the `run-lighthouse` label to produce a real end-to-end run and the authoritative (non-local) baseline numbers. None of these gate the code-level implementation, which is complete and correct either way — an unprotected preview or a preview without `noindex` just means the relevant conditional branch (bypass headers, `is-crawlable` exclusion) is a no-op rather than load-bearing.
- **Vercel Deployment Protection is real, and it needs the bypass secret in _two_ independent places.** The first live run of the job (`35253656170`) died in "Wait for Vercel preview": 401 on all 150 polls of the preview URL, then a timeout — Deployment Protection is enabled on this project, settling deferred item (1) above in the affirmative. Two separate HTTP clients hit those protected URLs, and neither configures the other, so both need the secret:
  1. `patrickedqvist/wait-for-vercel-preview`'s own readiness poller — `vercel_protection_bypass_header: ${{ secrets.VERCEL_PROTECTION_BYPASS }}` (`lighthouse.yml`, in the `wait` step; previously commented out "until confirmed").
  2. The real Chrome that `treosh/lighthouse-ci-action` drives — it gets nothing from the step above. `lighthouserc.cjs` now reads `process.env.VERCEL_PROTECTION_BYPASS` at module top level and, **only when non-empty**, spreads `extraHeaders: { 'x-vercel-protection-bypass': <secret> }` into `collect.settings`; the secret reaches it via `env: VERCEL_PROTECTION_BYPASS` on the "Run Lighthouse CI" step. Env-gated rather than unconditional so `make lighthouse` against a local `vite preview` (and any run without the secret) doesn't send an empty header.
     - **Header, not a query param, on purpose.** The alternative — appending `?x-vercel-protection-bypass=...` to the three `urls:` in `lighthouse.yml` — would leak the secret into `steps.lhci.outputs.links`, which `.github/scripts/lighthouse-comment.cjs` publishes verbatim in a public PR comment.
     - **`x-vercel-protection-bypass` is the real header name**, verified twice: Vercel's "Protection Bypass for Automation" docs, and `patrickedqvist/wait-for-vercel-preview@v1.3.3`'s `action.js` (it puts its input's value into exactly that header) — so both places use one secret and one header name.
     - **`x-vercel-set-bypass-cookie` deliberately not set.** Lighthouse applies `extraHeaders` via CDP `Network.setExtraHTTPHeaders`, so the header already rides along on every subresource request, not just the navigation; the cookie variant would only add a `Set-Cookie` redirect hop into the measured FCP/LCP.
     - **Object, not a JSON string, is the correct shape for `settings.extraHeaders`** — `@lhci/cli`'s `collect/node-runner.js` serializes `collect.settings` into a temp JSON file passed as `--cli-flags-path`, and `lighthouse@12`'s `cli/cli-flags.js` `coerceExtraHeaders` returns a `typeof value === 'object'` as-is without parsing.
  - **Confirmed live: the `VERCEL_PROTECTION_BYPASS` secret exists and works.** Creating it needed the Vercel Dashboard (Project Settings → Deployment Protection → Protection Bypass for Automation) and GitHub Settings → Secrets — a human did that after this section was first written. Job `35452468428` (PR #74) is the first real confirmation: "Wait for Vercel preview" got a `200` on the first poll (no more 401 wall), and `treosh/lighthouse-ci-action` successfully audited all 3 routes. If the secret is ever removed/rotated without updating GitHub, both places fall back to an empty string, `extraHeaders` stays inactive, and the job returns to failing on the same 401 wall — that's expected, not a config regression.
- **Trigger pattern mirrors `e2e.yml`.** `.github/workflows/lighthouse.yml` is its own workflow file with `on: pull_request: types: [labeled]`, gated on the `run-lighthouse` label (created on GitHub, same treatment as `run-e2e`) and `head.repo.full_name == github.repository` to exclude fork PRs — same rationale as E2E: keeps `ci.yml`'s shared `pull_request` trigger from re-running unrelated jobs, and keeps quota spend opt-in per PR rather than automatic.
- **PR-comment logic is extracted, not fully inline.** The sticky-comment/table-building logic that used to live entirely inside the `actions/github-script` step's inline `script:` block is now `.github/scripts/lighthouse-comment.cjs` (`buildCommentBody`, `findStickyComment`, plus a thin `run({ github, context })` orchestration wrapper that the workflow step calls via `require()` — the officially documented `actions/github-script` pattern for local scripts). The pure functions are covered by `.github/scripts/lighthouse-comment.test.mjs` (Vitest picks up `.test.mjs` via its default include glob — `.mjs`, not `.cjs`, because Vitest itself is ESM-only and can't be `require()`'d from a CommonJS test file; no `tsc`/tsconfig wiring needed since neither file is type-checked); `run()` itself stays untested — it would need a full Octokit mock, disproportionate for a thin wrapper. Same precedent as `sentry.config.ts`/`bundle.config.ts`: pull the testable logic out of an otherwise-untestable surface. **The "Comment PR with results" step also carries `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}`** (added after code review found it missing) — without it, the step silently skipped whenever the preceding "Wait for Vercel preview" step failed (Deployment Protection, timeout), so no comment was ever posted for that failure mode, contradicting the step's own purpose; `!cancelled()` (not a bare `always()`) still skips the step when the job itself is cancelled (e.g. by the `concurrency: cancel-in-progress` group), which a bare `always()` would not.
- **Two more regression tests added after code review**, closing gaps the initial implementation left: `font-swap.test.ts` (root) executes the real `public/font-swap.js` source via `node:vm` against a fake `document`/`link` to cover its three branches (no link present, already-loaded `link.sheet`, deferred-until-`load`), plus the `index.html`/`font-swap.js` id-coupling guard described under "Fonts" above; `src/app/styles/contrast.test.ts` recomputes the WCAG contrast ratio (relative-luminance formula) for the `--text-faint`/`--accent-warm` light-theme tokens fixed in Task 3, parsed directly from `global.css` rather than hardcoded, so a future accidental revert back toward the pre-fix hex values fails the test instead of only showing up on the next live Lighthouse run.
- **Two further test gaps closed after the PR #74 review.** (a) `contrast.test.ts` used to check `--accent-warm` only against the flat `--bg-secondary` (~5.57:1), but the active-filter states that actually failed axe render that text on the **translucent** `--accent-warm-soft` layered over `--bg-secondary` — `GenreSelector`'s `.chipActive`, `SearchSidebar`'s `.ratingBtnActive`, `Search.module.css`'s `.filterBtnActive`/`.typeBtnActive`, `ActiveFilterChips`' `.chip`. The composite measures **~4.52:1** — passing, but by 0.02, so the flat-only assertion would stay green while the real contrast slipped under 4.5. The file now parses the `rgba()` token too (`extractRgbaToken`) and alpha-composites it over the opaque backdrop (`compositeOver`, plain source-over blending, the same thing axe computes for an effective background) before measuring. `--bg-secondary` is the backdrop because it's what both containers hosting that combination use (`SearchSidebar.module.css`'s `.sidebar`, `BottomSheet.module.css`'s `.sheet`); `ActiveFilterChips` sit higher up on `--bg-primary`, where the same composite is ~4.97:1, so `--bg-secondary` is the worst real case. (b) `renderResultsTable` in `.github/scripts/lighthouse-comment.cjs` interpolated assertion values straight into markdown table cells — a single `|` or newline coming from an audited URL or an `actual` string would break the whole table in the PR comment. Cells now go through `escapeTableCell` (`|` → `\|`, CRLF/LF → `<br>`), covered by a `lighthouse-comment.test.mjs` case that feeds both characters through `buildCommentBody` and asserts one intact data row.

## Telemetry дашборд (Sentry)

Roadmap `2.5.7`. See `docs/plans/20260915-telemetry-dashboard-sentry-alerts.md` (moved to `docs/plans/completed/` once this task closes) for the full discovery/rationale (two review rounds, both with live `sentry` CLI/API checks, not memory/docs); this section captures the decisions that stick. Three independent layers: (1) Sentry Performance tracing, (2) telemetry-as-code (alerts + dashboard) provisioned via the `sentry` CLI, (3) Sentry MCP. Web Vitals moved here from Plausible (see [Analytics (Plausible)](#analytics-plausible) above) — this is also where LCP/INP/CLS now live.

- **Init order via `sentry-bootstrap.ts`.** `initSentry()` (`src/app/sentry.ts`) used to be called from `src/app/providers.tsx`; it's now called at module top level in `src/app/sentry-bootstrap.ts`, which `src/main.tsx` imports as its **first line**, ahead of `import { Providers } from './app/providers'` (both lines carry a WHY-comment warning the next editor not to reorder them, and `oxfmt`'s import sorter has been verified not to reorder a leading side-effect import). This isn't cosmetic: ES-module static imports of one module are fully evaluated, in source order, before that module's own body runs — so before this change, `providers.tsx`'s import of `./router` (which calls `createBrowserRouter(...)`) had already executed by the time `providers.tsx`'s body reached `initSentry()`. `Sentry.wrapCreateBrowserRouter` (see below) silently returns the router **unwrapped** if the router is created before `Sentry.init()` has run its `setup(client)` step — `node_modules/@sentry/react/build/esm/reactrouter-compat-utils/instrumentation.js`'s `createV6CompatibleWrapCreateBrowserRouter` checks internal `_useEffect`/`_useLocation`/`_useNavigationType`/`_matchRoutes` fields that only get set during that step, and its warning for the unset case is gated behind `DEBUG_BUILD` (stripped in prod) — so the bug was real and silent, not theoretical. `src/app/router.tsx` now wraps `createBrowserRouter` via `Sentry.wrapCreateBrowserRouter(createBrowserRouter)`.
- **Tracing integration.** `Sentry.init(...)` (`src/app/sentry.ts`) now also passes `integrations: [Sentry.reactRouterBrowserTracingIntegration({ useEffect, useLocation, useNavigationType, createRoutesFromChildren, matchRoutes })]` and `tracesSampleRate: SENTRY_TRACES_SAMPLE_RATE` (`= 0.2`, exported from `sentry.config.ts`, same "pure constant, unit-tested" pattern as `buildRelease`/`isSentryEnabled` — see "Error tracking (Sentry)" above). `reactRouterBrowserTracingIntegration` (not the `@deprecated` `reactRouterV7BrowserTracingIntegration`) plus `wrapCreateBrowserRouter` together group the parametrized `/movie/:id` route into one `/movie/:id` transaction name instead of one transaction per movie id — this was the exact blocker `2.5.1` deferred tracing over.
- **`tracesSampleRate = 0.2` and its trade-off.** 0.2 is the upper end of the range `2.5.1`'s "Как лучше" note suggested (0.1-0.2) — a balance between not burning Sentry's transaction quota on ordinary traffic and collecting enough samples for a reliable P75. **Two distinct risks, not one:** on very low traffic (a portfolio project), an alert's time window might simply gather _no_ samples at all — but there's a second, more insidious risk found in review: P75/`failure_rate()` computed over 1-2 sampled points in a window isn't "no signal," it's a **false** signal that looks like a real one, and Sentry Metric Alerts have no built-in minimum-sample guard for percentile/rate aggregates (the CLI has no flag for "don't alert below N samples"). The only available mitigation is operational: both `LCP_ALERT_WINDOW_MINUTES` and `ERROR_ALERT_WINDOW_MINUTES` (`sentry-telemetry.config.ts`) are deliberately widened to 60 minutes (not the more "responsive" 5-15 minutes) for the soak period, and every alert firing in the first 1-2 weeks should be eyeballed against real trace volume in the Sentry UI before being trusted — see Post-Completion tuning notes in the completed plan.
- **`tracePropagationTargets` is deliberately not passed to `Sentry.init(...)`** — the SDK default (same-origin/localhost only) is kept. Every API call goes to the absolute cross-origin `https://api.poiskkino.dev`, so `sentry-trace`/`baggage` headers wouldn't be attached there under the default anyway; widening the list buys nothing until distributed tracing to that API is actually wanted, and doing so first requires a live check that the third-party API's `Access-Control-Allow-Headers` permits those two headers (otherwise adding them breaks the request via a CORS preflight failure) — see `docs/telemetry-runbook.md` §4 for the exact condition to revisit this under.
- **Error-rate alert: `failure_rate()` Metric Alert, after two rejected designs.** The roadmap only says "alert on error rate > X%" — three designs were tried, in order, each rejected/superseded for a documented reason:
  1. **Issue Alert** ("issue seen by ≥10 unique users in 60 min") — rejected because `sentry alert issues create --condition`'s workflow-native JSON `type` for "unique user frequency" isn't documented or confirmed by a live call; adopting it would have meant an undocumented-format guess mid-task.
  2. **Count-based Metric Alert** (`count()` on the `errors` dataset ≥10/60min) — built as the Issue Alert's replacement, then found by external (Codex) review to be **semantically wrong**: an absolute count isn't a _rate_, contradicts "error rate" in both the roadmap wording and the alert's own name, and would fire on traffic growth alone rather than real degradation.
  3. **Final: `failure_rate()` Metric Alert on the `transactions` dataset** (`ERROR_RATE_METRIC_ALERT_CONFIG`, `sentry-telemetry.config.ts`) — the share of transactions with a status other than `ok`/`cancelled`/`unknown`. A real rate, no undocumented workflow-JSON needed, and it reuses the same transaction stream already collected for the LCP alert (one tracing pipeline, not a separate `errors`-dataset channel). **Open risk, unverified:** whether `@sentry/react`'s browser tracing actually flips a transaction's status on an uncaught JS exception in a pure SPA (server SDKs derive this from the HTTP status code, which a browser SDK has no equivalent of) — if `failure_rate()` reads as `0` on real production errors, the documented fallback is to rename the alert to an explicit "error count" Metric Alert (`count()` on `errors`), not silently keep a metric that never fires.
- **LCP P75 alert** (`LCP_METRIC_ALERT_CONFIG`) — `p75(measurements.lcp)` on the same `transactions` dataset, threshold `LCP_P75_THRESHOLD_MS = 2500` (the industry-standard Core Web Vitals "good" boundary), same 60-minute window and same statistical-significance caveat as above.
- **⚠️ Both Metric Alert builders currently produce argv that the real Sentry account rejects — documented as non-functional, not merely "unverified."** A live trial run (org `mycomp-ey`/project `kinoshka`, `sentry` CLI 0.44.1, 2026-09-16 — full log in the completed plan's Post-Completion section) found `sentry alert metrics create --dataset transactions` is rejected outright by the server for this account ("Creation of transaction-based alerts is disabled, as we migrate to the span dataset...", pointing at `dataset: events_analytics_platform`), while the CLI's own client-side validation doesn't accept `events_analytics_platform`/`eventsanalyticsplatform` as a `--dataset` value at all — its nearest accepted alternative, `--dataset spans`, is in turn rejected by the server as an invalid dataset for this query type. Separately, the trigger payload the server actually expects is wider than `--help` documents (`type`/`comparison`/`conditionResult` plus a mandatory second "resolve" condition — the account appears to be on a newer unified Detector/workflow format than CLI 0.44.1 documents). As a direct consequence, `ERROR_ALERT_FAILURE_RATE_THRESHOLD_PERCENT = 5` (`sentry-telemetry.config.ts`) is a **best-effort assumption** (0-100 scale, per Sentry's public docs for percentage aggregates) never confirmed by a successful live creation — the server rejects the request before that value is ever validated. `buildMetricAlertArgs` in `sentry-telemetry.config.ts` carries a `⚠️` docblock making this explicit so a future editor doesn't read "argv builder with a passing unit test" as "this works against the real account." Resolving this (CLI upgrade, manual UI creation + reverse-engineering the real payload, or waiting for Sentry to re-allow `transactions`-dataset alerts) is an open Post-Completion item, not resolved in this codebase.
- **Dashboard "Kinoshka Telemetry"** (`DASHBOARD_TITLE`, `DASHBOARD_WIDGETS` in `sentry-telemetry.config.ts`) — a 6-column grid: row 0 has three `big_number` widgets (failure rate, issue count, throughput; each 2×1), row 1 has two `line` widgets (LCP P75, INP P75; each 3×2), row 2 has two more `line` widgets (CLS P75, a throughput trend added purely to keep the row's width sum at 6, since a lone 3-wide CLS widget can't share a row with the full-width table below or stand alone without breaking the "row width sums to 6" invariant), and row 3 is a full-width (6×2) `table` of top issues. INP/CLS widgets carry a `TODO(Post-Completion)` — their `dataset`/`query` are a placeholder for visibility only (not a confirmed-working API call), since `@sentry/react` reports INP (and, on v9/v10, CLS) as standalone spans rather than transaction measurements, and the right dataset (likely `spans`/`events_analytics_platform`, not `transactions`) needs live ingested data to confirm. The roadmap only asks for an _alert_ on LCP — INP/CLS are dashboard visibility only, never alerted on.
- **Provisioning script: create-if-missing, not full sync.** `provision-sentry-telemetry.ts`'s `main()` resolves the team via a live `sentry team list <org>/ --json --fresh` call (not hardcoded, so it survives a team rename/recreation), then for each of the error-rate alert / LCP alert / dashboard: lists existing objects (`--json --fresh`, to bypass CLI caching that would otherwise break idempotency), checks `shouldCreate(existingNames, desiredName)` (`sentry-telemetry.config.ts` — a bare `!existingNames.includes(...)` by name), and only calls the real `sentry ... create`/`... widget add` (via an injectable `SentryRunner` — `{ json, run }`, defaulting to real `execFileSync`, swapped for a fake in tests) when the name isn't already present. **This is deliberately not idempotent in the stronger sense of "converges to the desired state":** if `sentry-telemetry.config.ts`'s thresholds change and the script is re-run, an already-existing alert/dashboard with the same name is left untouched — updating requires the manual `sentry alert metrics edit`/`sentry dashboard widget edit` path, not a script re-run. Dashboard widgets are only added on a dashboard's **first** creation; if that dashboard already exists, the script doesn't touch its widgets at all (neither re-creating nor diffing them). The widget-add loop wraps each `runner.run(...)` call in a `try`/`catch`: on failure it throws an error naming the widget that failed, its position (`N/total`), the remaining un-added widget names, and explicit manual-recovery instructions (add the rest by hand, or delete the dashboard and re-run) — because a partial failure leaves the dashboard already created (so `shouldCreate` will silently skip the whole widget block on a naive retry) and the CLI has no `dashboard widget list` to diff against.
- **`sentry-telemetry.config.ts` grammar notes reflecting review fixes:** `buildMetricAlertArgs`'s trigger action uses `targetIdentifier: ctx.teamId` as a **string**, not `Number(ctx.teamId)` — Sentry team ids are snowflake-like (16 digits in the live example) and could exceed `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`, which a JS `Number` would silently round; a string loses nothing here. `buildIssueAlertListArgs` was **removed as dead code** during Task 7's review — the design had already pivoted from Issue Alert to Metric Alert (`failure_rate()`) earlier, and `main()` never called it; it was leftover from before that pivot. `buildWidgetArgs(ctx, dashboardTitle, widget)` takes **three separate argv tokens** (`` `${ctx.org}/${ctx.project}` ``, then `dashboardTitle`, then `widget.name`) — an initial version concatenated `dashboardTitle` into one string with `org/project` (copying `buildDashboardCreateArgs`'s shape), but `sentry dashboard widget add --help`'s `ARGUMENTS` spells the target as `org/project/dashboard/title...`, which — cross-checked against the same "/"-in-argument-name convention used by `dashboard create`/`dashboard list`/`team list` — means several independent positional tokens, not one concatenated string; this was a real bug caught by re-verifying the final script against the live `--help` output, not a hypothetical.
- **`.mcp.json` / Sentry MCP.** Project-scoped, committed `.mcp.json` at the repo root: `{ "mcpServers": { "sentry": { "type": "http", "url": "https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp" } } }`. `mcp-config.test.ts` (root) reads and parses it, asserting `type === 'http'` and the URL _starts with_ `https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp` (not exact equality) — so a local, uncommitted narrowing to `/mycomp-ey/kinoshka` (see Post-Completion in the completed plan) doesn't break the test. OAuth authorization happens on first use inside a Claude Code session against this repo, not at commit time.
- **Runbook.** `docs/telemetry-runbook.md` documents the parts that aren't code: exact Plausible Custom Goal names for the four existing `trackEvent()` calls, an example conversion funnel, `sentry` CLI install/auth + `make sentry-telemetry` (including the dataset-rejection blocker above), and the `tracePropagationTargets` decision/revisit condition. This is where "PostHog/Plausible — conversion by key flows" (the roadmap's third `2.5.7` bullet) is actually closed — Plausible's tier in use has no API for goals/funnels, so this stays a manual UI runbook rather than code.

## Profile (`@features/profile`)

A client-only user profile, shipped ahead of Phase 5 (real auth/BFF) so the app has no dead "user" placeholders. See `docs/plans/completed/20260916-user-profile-block.md` for the full discovery/rationale; this section captures the decisions that stick.

- **Data.** The only profile field is a display name, stored as a plain string in `localStorage` under `kinoshka:profile` via `createStorageSlot` (`profileNameSlot`, `src/features/profile/model/profileStorage.ts`) — same pattern as `kinoshka:favorites`/`kinoshka:theme`/`kinoshka:genres`, including zod-validated reads (an invalid or over-long stored value degrades to `''`) and cross-tab sync. `useProfile()` returns `{ name, initials, setName, clearName }` (its result type is not exported from the barrel — nothing outside the hook needs it); `initials` is derived on every render by the pure `getInitials()` (`src/features/profile/lib/`), which is empty for an empty name so the UI can draw `ProfileIcon` instead of an empty circle. `clearName()` calls `profileNameSlot.set('')`, not `.remove()` — `remove()` doesn't notify `useStorageSlot` subscribers in the current tab. Both `setName` and `clearName` return the `boolean` that `set()` gives back (`false` on a failed write) — `clearName` used to discard it, silently making "Clear name" a dead control on a full/private-mode storage the same way "Save" used to be (see the storage-failures bullet below); `Profile.tsx`'s Clear handler now surfaces the same inline error on a failed clear. No favorites/theme data lives in the profile; the page just reads `useFavorites()`/`useTheme()`.
- **Length is counted in code points, `maxLength` is deliberately stricter.** The zod schema (`.refine(...)` on `Array.from(value).length <= PROFILE_NAME_MAX_LENGTH` and on the value being already trimmed), `normalizeProfileName()`'s truncation (`Array.from(trimmed).slice(0, N).join('')`, `profileStorage.ts` — moved out of `setName`/`useProfile.ts`, see the normalizer bullet below) and `getInitials` (`Array.from(word.toLocaleUpperCase())` — the first character is taken after upper-casing, so an expanding letter like `ß` → `SS` still yields one character) all work in code points so a surrogate pair (emoji) is never split in half. Grapheme clusters (flags, ZWJ sequences, combining marks) are several code points and are _not_ kept intact — accepted simplification, no `Intl.Segmenter`. The upper-casing uses a fixed `INITIALS_LOCALE = 'en'`, not the runtime default — pinning avoids the same name drawing different initials purely from the visitor's OS locale (Turkish/Azerbaijani would otherwise turn `i` into `İ`), while `'en'` still gives the same generic Unicode case mapping as no-locale for non-Latin alphabets (e.g. Cyrillic), so correctness there isn't lost. `getInitials` takes the first _visible_ code point of each word, not literally the first one — a word whose leading code point is invisible (see the normalizer bullet below) would otherwise itself become the initial, drawing an empty-looking circle for a non-empty name; `isInvisibleCodePoint()` (`src/features/profile/lib/visibleChars.ts`, next to `hasVisibleChar()` — both share one `INVISIBLE_ONLY` regex with `normalizeProfileName`/the slot schema in `model/profileStorage.ts`, which imports them from `lib/`; not part of the public barrel) is the single-code-point counterpart of the whole-name check the normalizer uses. The `<input maxLength>` attribute on `/profile` counts UTF-16 code units, so it is stricter than the schema (an all-emoji name is capped at half the limit through the UI) — accepted: the attribute is only a UI hint, and `setName`/the schema stay the source of truth for autofill/paste.
- **Names made only of invisible characters are rejected, and write/read share one normalizer.** `normalizeProfileName()` (`profileStorage.ts`, exported from the barrel) is the single normalization point: trim → truncate to 40 code points → trim again → `''` if no visible character is left (visible = not `\p{Cf}`/`\p{Cc}`/`\p{Zs}`/`\p{Zl}`/`\p{Zp}`/`\p{Default_Ignorable_Code_Point}`/U+2800). `setName` writes exactly its result and the zod read schema enforces the same rules, so anything `setName` stores round-trips (the earlier trim-after-slice regression was a write/read asymmetry). A ZWSP-only name would otherwise have rendered an empty avatar circle (no icon fallback) and an empty name line, and a screen reader would read "Your profile:" with nothing after. `Profile.tsx` compares the _normalized_ draft with the stored name for `isDirty` and resets the draft to the normalized value after a successful save.
- **Storage failures don't throw; they're surfaced to the user only on `/profile`, and reported to Sentry everywhere.** `createStorageSlot` (`@shared/lib`) wraps `localStorage` access in `try/catch`: `get()` falls back (a blocked-site-data `SecurityError` used to reach `GlobalErrorBoundary` on first render and blank the app), `remove()` is silent to the user (it only reports to Sentry, see below), and `set()` returns `boolean` (`false` on quota/private-mode failure, without notifying subscribers) instead of throwing — event-handler exceptions in React 19 don't reach an error boundary, so Save used to be silently dead. The signature change is backward compatible (`(value) => boolean` is assignable wherever `(value) => void` was used). **Not every caller surfaces the `false` to the user, and that's deliberate, not a gap:** `/profile`'s `useProfile().setName`/`clearName` do (see below), and `@features/favorites`'s `toggle()` gates its `trackEvent('favorite added')` call on the `boolean` too (a failed write no longer inflates the Plausible goal — see [Analytics (Plausible)](#analytics-plausible)), but theme/genre-dictionary callers still ignore it, same as before — a private-mode theme toggle or filter click stays a silent no-op in the UI. What changed for the _silent_ callers is that the failure is no longer invisible everywhere: a module-level error reporter, `setStorageErrorReporter()` (`@shared/lib`), is shared by all slots — it is not a `createStorageSlot` argument — and is unset (`null`) by default so tests/dev stay quiet; `get()` defers its report through `queueMicrotask` so `getSnapshot` stays a pure synchronous read, while `set()`/`remove()` report synchronously. Reports are deduplicated per `operation:key` with a 60-second cooldown (`REPORT_COOLDOWN_MS`, `storage.ts`) — not per-render, since a broken store would otherwise flood one event per write attempt, and not once-forever either, since a single early failure (e.g. a transient `QuotaExceededError`) would then silence a later, different failure of the same key/operation for the whole SPA session (bookkeeping only runs once a real reporter is installed). `src/app/sentry.ts`'s `initSentry()` wires it to `Sentry.captureException(error, { level: 'warning', tags: { storageKey, storageOperation } })` — the failing store's _key_ and _operation_ travel, never its value/content. This restores the signal `globalHandlersIntegration` used to pick up for free before the `try/catch` existed (an uncaught `QuotaExceededError`/`SecurityError` from an event handler used to reach Sentry on its own; the `try/catch` now catches it first).
- **Avatar initials use `--avatar-fg`, not `--text-primary`.** `--avatar-gradient` is dark in _both_ themes, but `--text-primary` inverts to a dark color in light: 2.74:1 / 1.47:1 against the gradient stops (`oklch(0.5 0.09 40)` / `oklch(0.35 0.06 20)`), failing WCAG AA. `--avatar-fg: #f2f0ef` is defined in both theme blocks of `global.css` (5.49:1 / 10.24:1, computed by hand — see below for why no tool confirms this) and used by `ProfileAvatar.module.css` and `Profile.module.css`. **This contrast is not covered by any automated check, on `/profile` or anywhere else, and can't be with the tooling this repo has today** — verified directly, not assumed: (a) Lighthouse (`lighthouse.yml`, `make lighthouse`) runs against a fresh browser profile with empty `localStorage`, so `useProfile().name` is `''` and both `ProfileAvatar` and `Profile`'s big circle render `<ProfileIcon />` — no initials text exists for axe to measure in that run at all; (b) even with a name set, `--avatar-gradient` is a `linear-gradient`, and axe-core's `color-contrast` rule can't compute an effective background through a gradient — it returns the check as `incomplete` ("Element's background color could not be determined due to a background gradient"), never as a violation or a pass, confirmed by running `@axe-core/playwright` against `/profile` with a name set: `results.violations` stays empty regardless of the actual contrast, so neither Lighthouse nor `e2e/utils/a11y.ts` (which only fails on `impact: 'critical'` violations, and `color-contrast` is `serious` besides) would ever flag a regression here — a `critical`-only gate on `violations` structurally can't, since this check never reaches `violations` for a gradient background. `/profile` is in the Lighthouse URL list (`lighthouse.yml`) for the rest of the page (headings, landmarks, form labels, focus order, non-gradient color-contrast, etc.) — that coverage is real, just not for the avatar. If this needs a real regression guard some day, the path is a `contrast.test.ts`-style unit test computed against the gradient's two solid stops (as the WHY-comment on `--avatar-fg` already does by hand) — not axe/Lighthouse, which structurally cannot see it.
- **`ProfileAvatar` is the second feature UI rendered from both header widgets** (after `ThemeToggle` from `@features/theme`) — `Header` and `MobileHeader` both import it from `@features/profile`, which is the legal `widgets → features` direction, so it lives in `@features/profile/ui/`, not `@shared/ui`. It is a `<NavLink to='/profile'>` (so it carries `aria-current='page'` on `/profile` itself) with `aria-label='Your profile'` (or `` `Your profile: ${name}` `` when a name is set — the initials alone would be read as a couple of letters). It replaced the hardcoded `<div className={s.avatar}>AV</div>` and the duplicated `.avatar` CSS in both header modules; the two old copies differed in `font-size` (10px vs 11px) and in `flex-shrink: 0` (only the `MobileHeader` one had it): the font size became the mobile-first base + `@media (min-width: 720px)` override on `.sm` in `AvatarCircle.module.css` (`@shared/ui`, which `ProfileAvatar` renders — `ProfileAvatar.module.css` styles only the `NavLink` wrapper), and `flex-shrink: 0` (`.avatar`, same file) is now applied unconditionally on purpose (the desktop header avatar gained it; harmless — it just never shrinks in the flex row). `MobileHeader` renders `rightAction ?? <ProfileAvatar />`, so `/movie/:id`'s "Share" button still overrides it; on `/profile` itself `MobileHeader` still shows the avatar (a link to the current page, marked `aria-current='page'`) — accepted redundancy, hiding it would need a new `RouteChromeConfig` field for one route.
- **The big avatar on `/profile` is not `ProfileAvatar`.** A link to the page you're already on is noise for a screen reader, so `Profile.tsx` renders its own decorative (`aria-hidden`) circle instead of `ProfileAvatar` (which is always a `<NavLink>`). Both call sites share the same visual circle — `AvatarCircle` (`@shared/ui`, `size: 'sm' | 'lg'`, takes `initials` and renders the `ProfileIcon` fallback when empty) — so the gradient/border/font styling isn't duplicated between `ProfileAvatar.module.css` and `Profile.module.css`; only the link-vs-decorative-div wrapping semantics (`aria-label` + `NavLink` vs `aria-hidden`) stay call-site-specific. `ProfileAvatar`'s own CSS module now styles only the `NavLink` wrapper (`text-decoration`/`:focus-visible`), not the circle itself.
- **No disabled auth stubs — including no disabled "Sign in".** Every control on `/profile` does something real: the name form (Save is disabled only while the _normalized_ draft equals the stored name), three quick links (`/favorites` with a count from `useFavorites().ids.length`, `/popular`, `/recommendations`), the Light/Dark/System radio group, and `Clear name` (rendered only when a name is set). The "sign-in will arrive with the backend" message is plain text, not a control — a disabled button would just reproduce the dead-placeholder problem this feature exists to remove. "My list / watched / ratings" are intentionally not implemented (no data source, no affordance elsewhere in the UI).
- **Draft resync: adjust-state-during-render, not `key={name}`.** `Profile.tsx` keeps a local `draft` for the input plus a `prevName` state; when the stored `name` changes (another tab via the `storage` event, `clearName()`, or `setName`'s own trim/truncation after a submit) `if (name !== prevName) { setPrevName(name); setDraft(name) }` runs during render. Without it the draft would go stale — Save would stay enabled and one click would overwrite a newer name with the old draft. `key={name}` on the form would also resync, but remounting drops input focus after the user's own submit, so it was rejected. The same branch also calls `setFailure(null)` — the single `failure: { action: 'save' | 'clear'; count }` state — so an in-flight error message, from a failed Save _or_ a failed Clear, doesn't survive a `name` change it no longer describes (e.g. another tab wrote a new name while the alert from _this_ tab's failed action was still up).
- **Save-error alert re-announces on a repeat failure; focus returns to the input after a successful save.** Two consecutive failed saves (no edit in between — the draft stays dirty against the still-unchanged stored name, so Save stays enabled) would otherwise leave the same `role='alert'` DOM node mounted for both, and most screen readers only announce a live region on its first appearance/text change, not on an identical re-render — so the second failure would go unannounced. `Profile.tsx` keys the alert `<p>` on `failure.count`, incremented on every failed `setName`/`clearName` call (not just the first), forcing React to unmount/remount a fresh node each time. Separately: a successful save disables the Save button (`isDirty` flips to `false`), and a successful clear unmounts the Clear button — a browser blurs a control the instant it becomes `disabled`/unmounted, so focus would otherwise silently fall to `<body>`. Both handlers call `restoreInputFocus()` after a successful write, so keyboard/mouse users keep their place; submitting via Enter from the input is unaffected (`focus()` on an already-focused input is a no-op). `restoreInputFocus()` skips the `focus()` when `matchMedia('(pointer: coarse)')` matches (a touchscreen primary pointer), since a programmatic focus there would pop the virtual keyboard open without the user asking for it. It deliberately uses a media query instead of tracking `pointerType`/keyboard activation on the Save button: WebKit doesn't focus a `<button>` on mouse click, so `document.activeElement`-based checks are unreliable, and hand-rolled interaction tracking was far heavier than the behavior justifies (trade-off: a hybrid touch laptop whose primary pointer is coarse won't get focus restored).
- **`--danger` token (`global.css`, both theme blocks) backs the save-error message, not `--accent-warm`.** `--accent-warm` is also the CTA/link/selected-theme-chip color, so the one error message on the page used to read as emphasis rather than failure. `--danger` is `#ff6b6b` (dark) / `#a33a2f` (light), each ≥4.5:1 (WCAG AA) against `--bg-secondary` — the `.header` section's background, where `.saveError` renders — the dark-theme ratio is a hand computation (same practice as the `--avatar-fg` bullet above), the light-theme one is regression-tested in `src/app/styles/contrast.test.ts` (that file only covers light theme, see its own header comment).
- **Embedded bidi override characters (e.g. U+202E RIGHT-TO-LEFT OVERRIDE) are accepted as part of a name, not stripped — a known, accepted cosmetic gap.** `normalizeProfileName`/the read schema reject a name only when _every_ code point is invisible (`hasVisibleChar`); a name that mixes an RTL override with visible letters (e.g. an RLO followed by ordinary Latin text) has a visible character, so it round-trips as-is and the browser renders it right-to-left. This is deliberately not "fixed" by stripping bidi controls: a blanket strip would also mangle legitimate RTL names (Hebrew, Arabic) that happen to need an explicit override for correct rendering next to a Latin word, and the impact here is purely visual/local (the stored string is unchanged, nothing is exfiltrated, no other user ever sees it) — not worth that risk for a cosmetic, single-user-visible edge case.
- **Appearance radio group is the first real consumer of `useTheme().theme`/`setTheme`** (before, only `toggleTheme`/`resolvedTheme` had callers, so `system` couldn't be chosen anywhere). It uses native `<input type='radio'>` inside `<fieldset>`/`<legend>` (keyboard and group announcement for free), with an `<h2>` inside the `<legend>` so the section is in the heading outline like `Quick access` (a bare `<legend>` isn't a heading). The header `ThemeToggle` is unchanged and still calls `toggleTheme()`, which always sets an explicit `light`/`dark` — so clicking it after choosing `System` on `/profile` replaces `system`; both controls share one `themeSlot`, so they never desync. This is deliberate (covered by a test), not a regression.
- **Routing/chrome.** `/profile` is a lazy `ProfilePage` route (`page-profile` chunk, see [Performance budgets](#performance-budgets--bundle-visualization)); `AppLayout`'s `ROUTE_CHROME['/profile']` is `{ active: 'profile', title: 'Profile' }` with no `activeNav` (`Header` has no profile nav-pill), so mobile shows a title instead of the search trigger, like `/favorites`/`/popular`/`/recommendations`.
- **`BottomNav` has no disabled items anymore.** Its `profile` item now navigates to `/profile` (it used to be `path: null`, disabled, with a test locking that in). The item type's `path` is narrowed from `string | null` to `string`, the `it.path &&` guard in `onClick` and the dead `.navItemDisabled` class are gone — reintroducing a disabled item means bringing that branch back on purpose. Tapping the item of the page you're already on navigates with `replace: `${pathname}${search}${hash}` === it.path` (i.e. the current URL has no query string or hash and its pathname equals `it.path`; no duplicate history entry); it compares against the URL, not with `active`, because `/movie/:id` has `active: 'search'` but tapping Catalog there must be a normal push. Comparing the whole `pathname+search+hash` string (not just `pathname`; added after a control-review finding) matters because every `it.path` is bare (no query string) while the actual current URL can carry one — e.g. `/search?q=matrix&genres=…`, since `BottomNav` mounts on `/search` too (`SEARCH_CHROME`): without it, tapping the already-active "Catalog" item there would `replace` the filtered URL with a bare `/search`, permanently erasing the filters from history (Back would no longer restore them). Comparing the whole URL string is still correct for the no-query routes (`/`, `/favorites`, `/popular`, `/recommendations`, `/profile`) — only `/search` carries a query string among `BottomNav`'s targets today.
- **Phase 5.** When a real session exists, only `useProfile()`'s data source changes (session instead of `localStorage`); the route, page, `ProfileAvatar`, `BottomNav` item and quick links are reused as-is (see `plans/roadmap.md`, Phase 5). Whether to migrate or drop the local `kinoshka:profile` name is a decision for the auth branch.
- **Out of scope, tracked in the backlog.** Other dead controls found next to the profile placeholders (header "Notifications" bell, movie-page "Share" button, static footer columns) are recorded in `docs/backlog/dead-header-controls.md`.

## Formatting

`formatCurrency()`/`formatDate()` (`@entities/movie/lib`) both take an optional second `locale` param that defaults to `navigator.language`, so money (`Budget`/`Box office`) and date (`Release date`) values in `DetailsTab`'s Details rows render in whichever language the visitor's browser is set to, instead of a hardcoded locale. Call sites never pass `locale` explicitly — only tests do, for determinism (jsdom's default `navigator.language` is `en-US`, so the default-locale assertions read as English output; ru-RU assertions pass the locale explicitly to prove the plumbing works). Any future formatter over an API-sourced numeric/date field should follow the same "explicit `locale` param, default to `navigator.language`" shape rather than hardcoding one.

## Data state

API integration is in progress, not all-or-nothing:

- **Live via `apiClient`:** the home feed rails consume `useNewMovies()` / `useTopRatedMovies()` (`@entities/movie`), which call `getMovies.ts` → `apiClient.getV15Movie(...)`. The `/search` page is **also live-data**: `Search` (the single mobile-first component, see [Responsive pattern](#responsive-pattern)) reads `?q`/filters/`?sort`/`?page` from the URL (single source of truth, via `useFilterState()` + native `useSearchParams()`) and render results through `useMovieCatalog()` — a facade hook in the **page slice** (`src/pages/search/model/useMovieCatalog.ts`, not `@entities/movie`, since it legally imports both `@features/catalog-filter` and `@entities/movie` downward). There is no `useSearch` hook (it was removed); `useMovieCatalog` routes by `query.trim()` between two mutually exclusive endpoints:
  - non-empty query → `getSearchMovies()` (`/v1.5/movie/search`, native `page`), filters/sort sidebar disabled (Variant A — the API can't combine free-text query with filters in one request). Disabling the sidebar is only cosmetic guard rail — the actual fix lives in `usePageSync` (`src/pages/search/model/usePageSync.ts`), which atomically strips `type`/`genres`/`yearFrom`/`yearTo`/`rating`/`sort` from the URL via `stripFilterAndSortParams` whenever text search becomes active (both on the `'' → non-empty query` transition, and on a deep link/refresh landing directly on `/search?q=...` with stale filter/sort params already in the URL — a mount-only effect handles the latter, since the transition-based effect only fires on a change between renders and never on first mount);
  - empty query → `getMoviesPage()` (`@entities/movie`), which drives `/v1.5/movie` (cursor-based, no native `page`) and **emulates numbered pagination** by walking the `next` cursor 1..N, memoizing each cursor step and the resulting page-level `Promise` for `use()`/Suspense stability.
  - The canonical genre filter value is the Russian `name` from the live genre dictionary (see the `useGenreDictionary()` bullet below) — exactly what `genres.name` expects, so `filtersToParams.ts` sends `filters.genres` straight through with no translation/skip step. Display labels go the other way: `src/features/catalog-filter/lib/genreMap.ts`'s `GENRE_LABELS` (RU→EN, inverted from the old EN→RU `GENRE_MAP`/`toApiGenre`) and `getGenreLabel(ruName)` fall back to the raw Russian name for dictionary genres with no known English label, rather than skipping them. Results from the API return Russian genre names as-is in `Movie.genre` (no reverse RU→EN mapping on display — accepted default, see `Search.tsx`). **Breaking change:** genre values in the URL used to be English (`?genres=Drama`); legacy links like that no longer match any dictionary entry (the chip renders as "active" but filters nothing) — no migration was done, since `?genres=` is a short-lived query param, not a long-lived contract (same principle as `Movie.genre` display above). See `docs/plans/20260815-dynamic-genre-dictionary.md`.
  - **Third live-data integration: the genre dictionary.** `useGenreDictionary()` (`@entities/movie/hooks`) backs the `GenreSelector` component (`@features/catalog-filter/ui`, one shared component rendered from both of `Search`'s two mounted-at-a-time filter variants — `SearchSidebar` (desktop) and the mobile filter bottom sheet inlined in `Search.tsx` — same "shared component, two call sites gated by the same `useViewport()` fork" pattern as `ActiveFilterChips`, see [Responsive pattern](#responsive-pattern)) — replaces the old hardcoded `ALL_GENRES` chip lists in both. It fetches `GET /v1.5/dictionary/genres` via `getGenreDictionary()` (`@entities/movie/api`) and caches the result in `localStorage` (key `kinoshka:genres`, 7-day TTL) through `createStorageSlot` (`@shared/lib`) — its first real consumer, which surfaced (and fixed) a referential-stability bug in `createStorageSlot.get()`: `get()` used to re-`JSON.parse` on every call, so for object/array values it returned a new reference each time; `useStorageSlot` passes `slot.get` straight into `useSyncExternalStore` as `getSnapshot`, which requires a referentially-stable snapshot between calls when the underlying store hasn't changed — otherwise React treats it as changed on every render, causing an infinite re-render loop plus React's "getSnapshot should be cached" dev warning. `get()` now memoizes the parsed value against the raw `localStorage` string and only re-parses when the raw string changes (see the docblock in `src/shared/lib/storage/storage.ts`); any future `createStorageSlot` consumer with an object/array value gets this for free. Genres change rarely, so this is a background-revalidate cache, **not** a Suspense/`use()`-blocking one: `useGenreDictionary()` is a plain synchronous hook that always returns immediately, either the cached dictionary or `STATIC_FALLBACK_GENRES` (6 genres) as a fallback, and kicks off a background `refreshGenreDictionary()` from a `useEffect` when the cache is empty or stale. A failed background fetch is cooled down (in-memory `lastAttemptAt`, 60s, not persisted) so a 403/500-ing endpoint doesn't get hammered — the filter stays usable on the static fallback either way. `invalidateGenreDictionary()` forces a cache clear/refetch. No `AsyncBoundary`/skeleton is needed for this piece of UI, unlike the other live-data integrations below.
  - `createCachedFetcher` (`@entities/movie/api/createCachedFetcher.ts`) was generalized from a fixed `Movie[]` result to `createCachedFetcher<P, R = Movie[]>` so both `getSearchMovies`/`getMoviesPage` (`R = { movies, totalPages }`) and the original `getMovies` rails (default `R = Movie[]`, unchanged call sites) share the same TTL/session-persist/403-cooldown cache. The returned fetcher also carries `invalidate(params)`/`clear()` (`Object.assign`'d onto the function) for point cache eviction — see the `AsyncBoundary`/retry note below.
  - **`useDeferredValue` never stages a stale value on data sourced from `useSearchParams()`, because `setSearchParams` wraps its navigation in `React.startTransition`.** `useCatalogUpdateStatus` (`src/pages/search/model/useCatalogUpdateStatus.ts`) drives the `/search` "keep showing old results while fetching" indicator (Suspense stale-content pattern, no `loader`s so `useNavigation()`/`useTransition()` don't apply here — see the plan referenced above). Naively calling `useDeferredValue(query)` etc. directly on values read from `useSearchParams()` never shows an intermediate stale render: the render where they change is already running in react-router's transition lane, React's internal `includesOnlyNonUrgentLanes` check sees that and hands back the new value immediately, so the deferred and live values change in the same commit and the "updating" indicator never lights up. The fix is to mirror the live values into a plain `useState` from inside a `useEffect` (effects run after commit, outside the transition, so the mirror update lands on the urgent lane) and run `useDeferredValue` over that mirror instead of the raw URL-derived values — see the hook's docblock for the full trace. This is a repo-wide gotcha, not specific to this one hook: any future `useDeferredValue` usage over `useSearchParams()`-derived state will hit the same silent no-op unless it goes through the same mirror-via-effect indirection.
  - **Shared "search → URL" contract, two entry points:** the home page's `HeroSection` (`src/pages/home/ui/HeroSection/HeroSection.tsx`) is a second entry point into `/search`, alongside `Header`. Both build the target URL from the same primitives — `filtersToSearchParams()`/`EMPTY_FILTERS` (`@features/catalog-filter`) for `type`, and `QUERY_MIN_LENGTH` (exported from `@widgets/header`, originally module-private to `Header.tsx`) as the shared min-length gate for `q` — instead of each hardcoding its own literal/threshold. `Header` writes `?q` live via debounce as the user types on an already-open `/search`; `HeroSection` writes the full URL once, on explicit submit (Enter or the "Search" button), since it lives on `/` and has no live results to update. Any future page-level search entry point should reuse this same pair of exports rather than re-deriving the min-length/param-building logic. See `docs/plans/20260814-home-hero-search-wiring.md`.
- **Also live-data: the movie-detail page (`/movie/:id`).** `MoviePage.tsx` calls `useMovieDetail(id)` (`@entities/movie/hooks`), which composes two independent fetchers via `Promise.allSettled`: `getMovieDetail()` → `apiClient.getV15MovieById(...)` (cast/crew/similar movies are fields on the same `MovieDtoV14`, not separate endpoints) and `getMovieImages()` → `apiClient.getV15Image(...)`. If `images` rejects, the hook swallows it and returns `images: []` so the page still renders; if `detail` rejects (including a 404), the rejection propagates to the `AsyncBoundary` around `MoviePage`. `MOCK_DETAIL` has been deleted from `@entities/movie`; `CATALOG` has also since been deleted — the mobile-first migration (`docs/plans/20260827-mobile-first-adaptive-layout.md`) moved the last mock-data content (formerly in `HomeMobile`) onto the same live rails the desktop home content already used, removing `CATALOG`'s only remaining consumer. `ALL_GENRES` has been removed entirely — its last two consumers (`SearchSidebar`, and what was `SearchMobile.tsx`, now the mobile filter variant inside `Search.tsx`) now render the live `GenreSelector`/`useGenreDictionary()` (see the genre dictionary bullet above).
  - **404/error-handling pattern (reusable for future pages):** the response interceptor in `src/shared/api/client.ts` rejects with `ApiError extends Error { status?: number }` instead of a bare `Error`, so callers can branch on HTTP status. `AsyncBoundary` (`@shared/ui`) takes an optional `errorFallback?: (params: { error: Error | null; reset: () => void }) => ReactNode` prop (default preserves the old single-`ErrorState` behavior); `MoviePage.tsx` passes a fallback that checks `error instanceof ApiError && error.status === 404` to render a distinct "not found" `ErrorState` (vs. a generic one for other errors), both wired to `onRetry={reset}`. Any future page needing to distinguish 404 from other failures should reuse this `ApiError` + `AsyncBoundary.errorFallback` pattern rather than inventing a new one.
  - **Retry really re-fetches:** `AsyncBoundary` also takes an optional `onRetry?: () => void`, invoked _before_ the underlying `reset()`. Double-click protection comes solely from a synchronous `isRetryingRef` flag set to `true` before `onRetry`/`reset` run and reset to `false` unconditionally on every `errorFallback` render (first error, a repeat render of the same cached error after a failed retry, or a genuinely new error) — not from comparing the `error` reference across renders, since real fetchers (`createCachedFetcher`/`getMoviesPage`) can replay the exact same cached `Error` object by reference on a retried request, which would otherwise leave Retry permanently dead instead of just cooldown-delayed. Each retry-capable async boundary wires `onRetry` to a companion `invalidate*` export sitting next to its data hook — `invalidateTopRatedMovies`/`invalidateNewMovies` (home rails), `invalidateMovieCatalog` (`/search`, via `useMovieCatalog.ts`), `invalidateMovieDetail` (`/movie/:id`, invalidates both `getMovieDetail`/`getMovieImages`) — so clicking Retry evicts that specific cache entry and hits the network immediately, instead of replaying the same rejected promise until `ERROR_CACHE_TTL_MS` (20s) expires.
- **Fourth live-data integration: `/popular` (rail + page).** `usePopularMovies()` (`@entities/movie/hooks`) is a Suspense hook over `getPopularMovies({ slug: 'popular', limit: 10 })` (`@entities/movie/api`), which calls `apiClient.getV15ListBySlug({ path: { slug }, query: { limit } })` → `GET /v1.5/list/{slug}`. The real slug is **`popular`**, not the `top10-week` the roadmap originally guessed — `GET /v1.5/list/top10-week` 404s, `GET /v1.5/list/popular` is the live one. Same status-narrowing pattern as `getMovieDetail.ts`: the endpoint's error DTO (401/403/404) carries `statusCode`/`message` instead of `movies`, so `getPopularMovies` checks `'statusCode' in response.data` and throws `ApiError` before touching `.movies`. Each `docs[]` item maps through the existing `mapDocToMovie()` plus `{ position, positionDiff }` into a new `PopularMovie = Movie & { position: number; positionDiff?: number | null }` type (`@entities/movie`) — `PopularMoviesRail` (home) and `PopularPage`'s `Popular` component both render it, with `MovieRail`/`Card` taking an optional `rankBadge`/`PopularBadge` slot for the position number and signed `positionDiff` (rendered as a plain signed integer, no up/down arrow — the API doesn't document which sign means "rose" vs "fell"). `MovieInListDto` (the `/list` endpoint's movie shape) **lacks `type`/`genres`**, unlike `SearchMovieDtoV14` — `mapDocToMovie` falls back to its existing defaults (`type: 'movie'`, `genre: []`), so every popular-list card shows a generic `'movie'` type badge; this is an accepted default, same principle as the RU-genre-display one described above for search results, not a bug to fix. `createCachedFetcher` (`@entities/movie/api/createCachedFetcher.ts`) gained an optional third `options?: { ttlMs?: number }` param (default unchanged: 5 minutes) specifically so `getPopularMovies` could opt into a 24-hour TTL — `24 * 60 * 60 * 1000` ms, passed as `{ ttlMs: ... }` — since a curated "popular this week" list changes far less often than the other rails. **That 24h TTL is in-memory-only in production**: `createSessionCache` (backing `createCachedFetcher`) only persists to `sessionStorage` under `import.meta.env.DEV` (see the Testing note below and `src/shared/lib/sessionCache/sessionCache.ts`), so in prod the cache survives re-renders/navigation for the life of the SPA session but not a page reload — still useful for staying under the demo tier's 200-requests/day quota during a long session.
- **Client-only (no API endpoint): Favorites.** `@features/favorites`'s `useFavorites()` stores the favorited id set as `number[]` in `localStorage` (key `kinoshka:favorites`) through `createStorageSlot` — same pattern as `kinoshka:genres` (see the genre dictionary bullet above), including zod-validated reads with an empty-array fallback and cross-tab sync via the `storage` event. The theme feature (`@features/theme`) follows the same `createStorageSlot` pattern for its own key, `kinoshka:theme` (see the theming pattern note under [Component structure](#component-structure)). There is no favorites API endpoint; loading the favorited movies' full data is a client-side composition, not a live-data integration in the sense of the bullets above: `getMoviesByIds()` (`@entities/movie/api`) calls the existing `getMovieDetail(id)` per id via `Promise.allSettled` (partial failure — a 404'd id just drops out of the result) and is wrapped in `createCachedFetcher<number[], Movie[]>`, cache-keyed on the id array itself so it naturally invalidates whenever the favorited set changes. `useFavoriteMovies()` (`@features/favorites`) is the Suspense-style `use()` wrapper around it, meant to render inside an `AsyncBoundary` — same shape as the other `use()`-based data hooks in this codebase. `Card` takes optional `isFavorite`/`onToggleFavorite` props (both undefined → no heart button rendered, preserving old behavior for not-yet-wired call sites) rather than importing `@features/favorites` directly, since `entities/movie` can't import upward from `features/` under this repo's FSD import direction — callers in `widgets/`/`pages/` call `useFavorites()` themselves and pass `isFavorite`/`toggle` down as props.
- **Fifth live-data integration: `/recommendations` (rule-based, no new API layer).** `computeRecommendationQuery(favorites: Movie[]): NonNullable<CatalogParams> | null` (`@features/recommendations/lib`) is a pure rule — top-3 favorited genres by frequency, average favorited rating minus a −1 buffer (floored at 0) as `rating.kp`, and `id: ['!<id>', ...]` to exclude already-favorited movies — that turns the favorited set into a `CatalogParams` query. There is no dedicated recommendations endpoint or API wrapper: the query is handed straight to the same `getMoviesPage()` (`@entities/movie`) that `/search`'s empty-query path already uses, for free reuse of its cursor-pagination cache, TTL, and 403-cooldown. `favorites: Movie[]` (from `useFavoriteMovies()`) is itself Suspense data, so — same FSD reasoning as `useMovieCatalog` (see the "Page-slice `model/` facade" note above) — the favorites+rule composition can't live in `@entities`/`@features` and instead lives in `src/pages/recommendations/model/useRecommendedMovies.ts`: `useRecommendedMovies(): Movie[] | null` calls `useFavoriteMovies()` → `computeRecommendationQuery()` → (if non-null) `use(getMoviesPage(query, 1)).movies`, returning `null` when the rule itself can't produce a query (empty favorites) as distinct from `[]` (query ran, catalog had nothing to offer). The companion invalidator `invalidateRecommendations(ids: number[])` — analogous to `invalidateMovieCatalog` — lives in the same file: since the rule's input (`favorites`) is itself async and not synchronously available at the `AsyncBoundary`'s `onRetry` call site (unlike `useMovieCatalog`, where `filters`/`sort`/`page` are ordinary synchronous props), the hook remembers the last computed `query` in a module-level variable as a render side effect and the invalidator uses it to evict both `getMoviesByIds`'s cache entry and `getMoviesPage(lastQuery, 1)`'s.
  - **Naming: `useRecommendedMovies`, not `useRecommendations`.** Roadmap 2.4's literal wording says "Хук `useRecommendations()`", but the implementation deliberately deviates: `useFavorites()`/`useFavoriteMovies()` already establish the project convention that `use<Domain>` returns raw/underlying data while `use<Domain>Movies` is the Suspense hook that resolves to `Movie[]`. `useRecommendedMovies` follows that existing convention instead of the roadmap's literal name.
  - **Feature flag not wired.** `FeatureName` in `src/shared/config/features/useFeatureFlag.ts` already lists `recommendations: false` with no consumer. This page is intentionally not gated behind that flag — same precedent as `popularThisWeek`/`toggleTheme`, both left `false` in the same map after their features shipped.

When adding a new feature, check whether an equivalent live-data hook already exists before reaching for mock data.

**Testing:** API calls are mocked in tests via **MSW** (`msw/node`, `setupServer()` in `src/test/setup.ts`, `onUnhandledRequest: 'error'`). Vitest config lives inline in `vite.config.ts` (`test: { environment: 'jsdom', setupFiles: [...], globals: true }` — `globals: true` means `describe`/`it`/`expect` need no import). **Zod** validates data at the localStorage/sessionStorage boundary only — API responses are trusted as-is against the generated types (no Zod schema), matching `getMovies.ts`/`getSearchMovies.ts`/`getMoviesPage.ts`/`getMovieDetail.ts`/`getMovieImages.ts`/`getGenreDictionary.ts`.
